chunks: From him, from Abu Ja'far, from his father, from Wahb, from Ja'far, from his father, peace be upon them, that Ali (peace be upon him) said:
The Mudabbir (slave manumitted upon owner's death) is not sold except from his own self (i.e., using his own money).

key_terms.الْمُدَبَّرُ: A slave whose manumission is contingent upon the owner's death
key_terms.مِنْ نَفْسِهِ: From his own self (using his own money/assets)

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on selling a Mudabbir slave in Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: This hadith from Imam al-Sadiq (AS), transmitted through the chain of Ali (AS), clarifies the legal status of the *Mudabbir* (slave manumitted upon the owner's death) by restricting their sale to transactions funded by their own capital. This ruling underscores the principle of financial autonomy for the *Mudabbir*, ensuring that the path to freedom is not obstructed by external owners' arbitrary decisions, a key topic in Shia jurisprudence regarding manumission (*Tadbir*).
